title: Minimum speed to escape a body's gravity
references: Kleppner, D. and Kolenkow, R. J., An Introduction to Mechanics, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press (2014)
IAU 2015 Resolution B3 on recommended nominal conversion constants for selected solar and planetary properties, arXiv:1510.07674
validity_domain: A body launched at distance r from the centre of a spherically symmetric mass with gravitational parameter GM escapes to infinity only if its launch speed is at least sqrt(2 GM / r), when no further propulsion acts on it (Newtonian gravity, energy conservation).
limitations: Assumption propulsion: under ballistic (no further propulsion) the launch speed must be at least sqrt(2 GM / r); under powered flight this law gives no bound (the bound used is 0).
Speed in the inertial frame of the body's centre: a launch along the rotation of the body gains its surface speed (about 0.46 km/s at Earth's equator)
Atmospheric drag and the pull of other bodies are ignored; drag only raises the speed needed
Newtonian: not valid near a black hole

variables.GM: Gravitational parameter of the body (G times its mass)
variables.r: Distance from the body's centre at launch
